chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Husayn al-Ahmasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who departs from Makkah while not intending to return to it, his term has drawn near and his punishment has approached.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of intending to return to Makkah after Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the physical departure from Makkah without the intention of return to the nearness of death, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that Makkah serves as a spiritual anchor and a place of divine refuge. This hadith underscores the virtue of maintaining a lifelong spiritual connection to the Sacred House, viewing it not merely as a destination for ritual but as a permanent abode of the heart. The warning implies that severing this emotional and spiritual tie accelerates the soul's journey toward its final reckoning.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Husayn Al Ahmasy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who goes out from Makkah (after performing Hajj or Umra) and he does not intend the return to it, so he has brought his term (death) closer, and his Punishment would be closer’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Husayn al-Ahmasiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
one who leaves Makkah with an intention not to return to Makkah again, (must take notice that) his death has come very near, as well as torment for him.”
